result.title: Psychometrics-Inspired Coreset Selection for Image Quality Assessment
result.summary: Collecting large-scale subjective annotations remains a critical bottleneck in training accurate image quality assessment (IQA) models. Coreset selection reduces this burden by selecting representative images before annotation. However, diversity in a visual feature space does not necessarily reflect diversity in perceptual quality, raising a fundamental question about which quality-related factors the representation should encode. We propose GRAM, a quality-aware representation learning framework inspired by the graded response model (GRM) from psychometrics. GRM describes how an individual's latent ability determines the probabilities of reaching successive assessment grades, with response sensitivity and grade thresholds governing this relationship. In this paper, we find that this principle naturally aligns with perceptual quality assessment, where the impact of image degradation depends on image content and distortion characteristics. Building on this connection, GRAM models quality judgments through three complementary factors: latent quality, content-dependent response sensitivity, and distortion-dependent grade thresholds. These factors jointly determine the probabilities of attaining different quality grades and the resulting expected quality score. The learned parameters provide a structured quality-aware representation that complements general visual features for coreset selection. Experiments on nine datasets demonstrate improvements across different selection strategies, downstream IQA models, and annotation budgets. The code will be made publicly available.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 GRAM，借鉴心理测量学的分级反应模型，把图像质量判断分解为潜在质量、内容相关的响应敏感度与失真相关的分级阈值，学习质量感知表示用于标注前的 coreset 选择，并在九个数据集上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「潜变量—敏感度—阈值」的测量模型式分解，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态的刻画、分级读出与训练样本筛选提供概念线索，但该工作面向 IQA 标注预算，与多模态推理无直接联系，具体可迁移性需核查。
